prompt: A jacket priced at $\$80$ is marked up by $15\%$. What is the new price, in dollars?
hint: A markup adds a percent of the price on top of the full original price. What percent of the old price is the new price?

hints.text: A markup adds a percent of the price on top of the full original price. What percent of the old price is the new price?
The new price is $100\% + 15\% = 115\%$ of the old price, so multiply: $80 \times 1.15$.
Since $80 \times 1.15 = 92$, the new price of the jacket is $92$ dollars.

learningObjective: Apply a percent increase using a single multiplier.
explanation: A $15\%$ markup keeps the original $100\%$ and adds $15\%$ more, so the multiplier is $1.15$.
Multiply the original price by that number: $80 \times 1.15 = 92$.
Finding the increase separately gives $0.15 \times 80 = 12$ and $80 + 12 = 92$. The new price is $92$ dollars.

alternativeExplanations.title: The multiplier method scales better
steps: One multiplication ($\times 1.15$) replaces two steps, and there is no risk of forgetting to add the increase back.
It also chains: two successive $15\%$ increases are just $\times 1.15$ twice.
Get comfortable converting a percent change to a multiplier — it is the backbone of this entire unit.
